rows: What caused the Golden Age (1945-73)?
Reconstruction catch-up + Keynesian demand management + cheap oil + US hegemony + labor-capital bargain
MITI's main tools?
Credit allocation to priority industries + import protection + technology licensing + recession cartel organization
What is the "flying geese" model?
Japan leads industrialization; Korea/Taiwan follow as Japan moves to higher value-added; structural upgrading in sequence
ISI vs EOI key difference?
ISI protects without export requirements; EOI in East Asia made protection contingent on export performance
What broke the Phillips curve in 1973?
Supply-side oil price shock: both inflation AND unemployment simultaneously; demand-side tools can't fix supply-side shocks
OPEC mechanics?
Production quotas among members; supply restriction; Middle East oil low cost means cartel profit enormous
Volcker shock: what and when?
October 1979; Fed switched to targeting bank reserves; FFR rose to 20%; broke inflation at cost of deep recession
When did US manufacturing employment peak?
~1973 at 25% of workforce; now ~9%
Financialization measure?
Financial sector's share of corporate profits: ~10-15% (1950s-60s) to ~30-40% (2000s)
What exhausted the Golden Age?
Catch-up growth exhausted + oil shock + Bretton Woods breakdown + labor power peak + productivity slowdown
